knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The guideline gives general wards as the significant-risk example. Intensive care sits in the high-risk level, and rehabilitation and office settings sit in the low-risk level.
The table sets a daily minimum for door handles in patient rooms at the significant level. Twice daily is the highest level; weekly and monthly are too infrequent.
The table gives minimum frequencies. Extra cleaning after soiling is a normal part of the work. The other options misread the table.

practicalCriteria: Learner identifies the risk level for the assigned area and reads the frequency for three high-touch items.
Learner logs two cleans against the correct items and times.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: The risk level for the area is unclear
A visible body substance is on a high-touch item and no spill procedure is available
